call_input.prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing.
Create exactly ONE finished flat Korean title-only poster, portrait 2:3, full-bleed artwork. No mockup, frame, panels or contact sheet.
요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력.

Core relationship: night growth opens and becomes visible as light passes through the absence of a dense dark plant structure. Build ONE continuous connected botanical figure-ground matrix, organized by one large enclosing dark form and its widening openings. The image and the Korean title must both be negative knockouts revealing the same cool pale underlying light. This is a poster about a flower opening at night, not a floral wallpaper with a heading.

Concrete image construction: use smooth, solid near-black midnight violet shapes over a cool pale yellow-green ground. A dense enclosing mass of broad tapered leaves, joined branching stems and folded petal shapes fills the poster. Its biggest dark folds curve around one asymmetrical opening in the upper half, like a flower loosening from a nearly closed night enclosure. Five varied petal-shaped slits open and broaden outward from an off-center pale heart. The dark folded forms between those slits are visibly botanical petals turning apart, so their negative gaps reveal an open bloom. Keep the enclosing shape substantial at the top and left, then let the largest pale opening widen toward the upper-right. The light is completely flat unprinted-looking absence in the dark silhouette, never a glow or a spotlight. Use only this one major bloom opening; lower down, a single small tightly closed dark bud joins the same branching stalk. Broad leaves and a few narrow branching voids tie all these shapes into one growth structure extending to the lower and side edges. Deliberately vary aperture size and direction. Avoid repeated flower emblems, repeated radial rosettes, detached stamens, or scattered floral ornaments. No ground plane, horizon, vanishing point or ordinary garden depth.

Typography: cut the title out of the same contiguous dark botanical mass as clean pale negative openings. Place it on one steady horizontal baseline in the lower-middle, around two-thirds down the canvas, large enough to read at thumbnail size, approximately four-fifths of the poster width. Use bold compact Korean sans-serif glyphs with complete regular syllable construction, clear counters and even stroke strength. Keep a normal clear word space after the first two-syllable group and after the second two-syllable group; the two spaces must visibly exceed the syllable gaps and be similar in width. Do not draw leaves onto the lettering or turn letters into vines. Around the title, maintain the large enclosing dark form and changing botanical edges, rather than clearing a horizontal lane, rectangular box, banner, title stripe or independent text panel. Plants and light apertures must stop short of every glyph's intact outer contour and counters. The title itself is the pale cutout, with no shadow, outline, extrusion or added rectangle.

Reading path: first discover the dark enclosure opening into a bloom, then read the intact negative Korean title as another opening in that same field, then follow the single branching growth structure toward its closed bud. Strong unequal areas of enclosed darkness and widening pale voids convey night and opening. The entire layout must be legible as one garden structure with large controlled forms; do not fill every remaining gap with decoration.

Text (verbatim, print once and only once): "밤에 피는 정원"

Only those exact Korean syllables and their two word spaces may be printed. No quotation marks, extra words, translation, subtitles, captions, numbers, dates, labels, logos, watermark, symbols or ornamental marks. Single flat poster, exact 2:3 portrait. Smooth solid planar shape edges; no automatic paper texture, simulated print wear, speckles, gradients, glass, metallic material, 3D volume, glow, rays, moon, stars, or photographic lighting. The negative light openings and intact title, not surface effects, must make the garden visible and the flower's opening perceptible.

residuals: Conventional horizontal title can still read as a heading inside a broad dark leaf, despite shared negative openings.
Upper bloom can read as a pale silhouette as well as absence within a dark enclosure.
Night is abstractly conveyed through dark enclosure and pale voids; nocturnal opening is not independently naturalistically demonstrated.
Faint planar tonal variation and a few pinched acute petal turns remain.
